messages.text: MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year joins Hundred final coverage

metadata.summary: The MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year for 2026, Rosa Simkin, received the ultimate competition prize when joining Sky Sports' live coverage of The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday.
metadata.content: Rosa Simkin: 2026 MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year winner joins Sky Sports for The Hundred final at Lord's | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Rosa Simkin: 2026 MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year winner joins Sky Sports for The Hundred final at Lord's MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year winner for 2026 is Rosa Simkin; the 18-year-old from Warwickshire, who is currently studying yournalism at Cardiff University, joined Sky Sports' live coverage of The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday as part of her prize Monday 17 August 2026 14:28, UK Image: Rosa Simkin interviews Trent Rockets' Georgia Adams for Sky Sports during The Hundred women's final at Lord's (image: Jed Leicester, MCC ) The MCC Female Young Broadcaster of the Year for 2026, Rosa Simkin, received the ultimate competition prize when joining Sky Sports' live coverage of The Hundred final at Lord's on Sunday. During the innings break of both the women's and men's finals, Rosa held flash interviews talking to Georgia Adams from Trent Rockets and Noor Ahmad from Manchester Super Giants as both teams ultimately went on to lift the titles. The 18-year-old also presented some of the bitesize highlight videos for Sky Sports Cricket's digital channels and made content for Lord's Instagram, giving audiences an insight into her day as part of the team. messages.text: How Hunt struck gold with historic Championships display

metadata.summary: Amy Hunt told Sky Sports back in February that three gold medals in Birmingham was the dream. Six months later, she is a four-time European champion and the first athlete to win four golds at a single European Championships.
metadata.content: Amy Hunt: How British sprinter surpassed her own goal for gold with historic four-medal display at European Championships | Athletics News | Sky Sports Skip to content Amy Hunt: How British sprinter surpassed her own goal for gold with historic four-medal display at European Championships British sprinter Amy Hunt won an incredible four gold medals at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham; Sky Sports examines how the Cambridge-educated athlete came through challenges during the pandemic to secure glory in front of her home fans Ellie Prophet Sports Journalist Monday 17 August 2026 15:46, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Amy Hunt reflects on her record-breaking European Championships, after the Team GB sprinter secured four gold medals. Amy Hunt told Sky Sports back in February that three gold medals in Birmingham was the dream. Six months later, she is a four-time European champion and the first athlete to win four golds at a single European Championships. Hunt held up four fingers to the camera after winning gold in the mixed 4x100m relay, completing her historic haul. When Sky Sports spoke to the sprinter in February, the World and Olympic silver medallist was looking ahead to Birmingham and the chance to impress on home soil. metadata.summary: Nasser Hussain hailed new England Test captain Joe Root's decision to abolish a team curfew but fears the returning skipper sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader like his predecessor Ben Stokes.
metadata.content: Joe Root: England Test captain right to remove curfew, says Nasser Hussain ahead of three-Test Pakistan series | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to content Joe Root: England Test captain right to remove curfew, says Nasser Hussain ahead of three-Test Pakistan series Nasser Hussain: "I'm pleased Joe is doing it [Test captaincy], although I may have gone in the direction of Harry Brook"; watch the first Test of the three-match series between England and Pakistan, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 10am, Wednesday (first ball 11am) Nasser Hussain Cricket expert and columnist Monday 17 August 2026 14:29, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England Test captain Joe Root explains why he has removed the curfew that was previously imposed on his team Nasser Hussain hailed new England Test captain Joe Root's decision to abolish a team curfew but fears the returning skipper sometimes lacks a feel for the game as a leader like his predecessor Ben Stokes. Root has captained England on a record 65 occasions, most recently during their second Test defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after Stokes and Gus Atkinson were suspended for breaking a team curfew that was introduced off the back of the 4-1 Ashes defeat in the winter. Perhaps the gaping holes through the spine of his team should be more of an immediate area of focus. The manner of that loss has raised qualifying questions, the only real clarity offered by the Premier League champions. Mikel Arteta's side brutally exposed a series of City shortcomings: defensively disorganised, missing a midfield and lacking leadership, to name but a few. Under a week from the start of their campaign proper, City appear worryingly incomplete.
